findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §7 step 5, against §7 preamble, §2 material-decision rule, §9 exceptions table and docs/contracts/integration-authorization.md
findings.what: Step 5 lets acceptance of the verified staging identity be performed by "закреплённая auto-policy", while the same section's preamble ("Project policy integration не разрешает"), §2 ("integration решения всегда требуют пользователя"), §9 ("project alignment policy запрещена") and the class `integration_authorization_policy_issued` all exist to forbid exactly that, so the last human control before a user's branch moves is specified two contradictory ways.

The registry instance `resources/artifact-registry/artifact-registry.v1.json` is named by exact path as the classifier whose `registry_digest` every editorial Code-Review exemption records and whose classes decide every path's lifecycle ("реестр решает"), but only `artifact-registry.schema.json` is among the 109 candidate files — while the sibling instances `refusal-vocabulary.v1.json` and `stage-carriers.v1.json` are present — so the deciding authority is outside the attested candidate and, taken literally, every path is `unregistered_artifact`.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §2 and §8 vs the 37 closed sets in section 4
findings.what: The four named alignment lifecycles are the design's primary human-authority gate, yet no contract among the 37 covers them, and their stop reasons `brief_alignment_required`, `core_flow_decision_required`, `tech_plan_readiness_required`, `alignment_policy_out_of_scope`, `alignment_record_stale`, `artifact_mapping_required`, `arena_fallback_required`, `protocol_lock_invalid` and `implementation_scope_invalid` appear in no closed refusal set in section 4 — only the sibling `tickets_breakdown_alignment_required` does (tickets-manifest.md) — although refusal-vocabulary.md §3 says the vocabulary is extracted from contracts, not maintained.

findings.where: 02-architecture.md §6 (ADR-029 envelope) vs docs/contracts/provider-preflight.md and docs/contracts/project-instructions-lock.md refusal sets
findings.what: The guarantee that the provider's own auto-context is "либо отключён, либо целиком перечислен lock'ом" has no enforcing class: provider-preflight's 11 classes cover route/auth/effort/permission-mode/smoke and nothing about context ingestion, and project-instructions-lock's 10 classes cover discovery/drift/identity of the lock file, not what the provider loads by itself — so unpinned bytes entering the envelope would silently void the protocol-hash and PASS bindings [INFERENCE: both contract bodies are digest-only here, so a clause could exist that section 4's class list does not surface].

findings.where: section 5, fault matrix F001–F016 vs 01-core-flows.md §2 and 02-architecture.md §2/§5
findings.what: The 16 injected groups contain no fault in the daemon authority/decision-journal domain (signed `UserDecisionRecord` crash-tail: journal-ahead accepted only after byte-exact signature verification, nonce not released, invalid tail quarantined) and none for the live→audit custody window that 02 §2 singles out ("crash between `audit_ref_verified` and `live_ref_deleted` resumes this exact record"), so `covered_by_real_fault=16; complete=true` is complete over the chosen enumeration while the two recovery invariants the whole authority model rests on are unexercised.

The mutated set is five literal call-site tokens (`demand(`, `errors.push(`, `reasons.push(`, `findings.push(`, `problems.push(`), so 512/512 shows only that each emission site is observed by some test — no predicate, boundary or control-flow mutant exists and any guard not written in those shapes is untouched — and "modules covered: 49" is given with no denominator in a package that supplies one for the fault matrix; "survivors: 0, all named in resources/mutation-report/mutation-survivors.v1.json" is also self-contradictory phrasing for an empty set.

Under `pull_request`, `merge_queue` or `fork_pull_request` the host explicitly does not move the branch, so step 7's CAS and step 8's post-CAS re-read never run, yet step 10 makes `done` conditional on step 8 and the flow names no terminal state for the profile-routed path [INFERENCE: delivery-profile.md §6a plus `completion_predicate_unmet` probably resolves it, which means the full-text flow contradicts the digest-only contract].

The staging ref is written `refs/autosk/epics/<epic-id>/staging` using the raw display id, while planning and candidate refs under the same helper-owned `refs/autosk/**` prefix are keyed by `<epic_ref_key>` = domain-separated SHA-256 of `{project_root_sha256, epic_id}` with the explicit warning "Это не display ID и не пользовательский slug", so one namespace has two key conventions and the integration-critical one carries no project binding and no guaranteed ref-name validity.

The flow declares the five-way path-role classifier unreachable in the delivered system because the registry decides, but the architecture still derives `governance_mapping_set_digest` — a field of candidate identity and therefore of every verdict binding — from that classifier emitting `ordinary_implementation`, so an identity input depends on a rule the other document says nothing can reach.

"Supplementary" (Opus/GPT/Grok/Kimi supplementary) is never defined anywhere in the reproduced text, yet synthesis requires a valid answer from all four seats and the scale says any Critical or High blocks, so an artifact's own author family occupies a counting seat whose authority to block or to clear is unstated.

findings.where: section 5, "What is not claimed" (issue #10 criterion 2) vs docs/contracts/refusal-vocabulary.md §4
findings.what: Deferring the declarative workflow graph is defensible as scope, but refusal-vocabulary.md §4 promises "a park reason parks at a step that exists" and closes on `refusal_vocabulary_unknown_step`, and no artifact in section 3 is a step registry — 01 §8's hand-maintained resume table is the de-facto one — so step existence is validated against prose rather than against the transition table the runtime executes, and that pairing (defer the graph, keep the guarantee) is the defect rather than the deferral itself.

findings.where: section 4 headline ("378 refusal classes") vs the per-contract sets
findings.what: 378 counts declarations, not distinct names: `registry_drift` is declared by both artifact-registry.md and finding-registry.md and `foreign_ref_movement` by both approved-delta.md and execution-base.md, while refusal-vocabulary.md binds each reason to one registered step and one producer (`refusal_vocabulary_producer_missing`/`_misdeclared`), so a name owned by two contracts cannot have a single producer or step.

Arena gates Tech Plan changes and the extension mechanically extracts the `autosk-arena` block, but Arena has neither a contract among the 37 nor a schema among the resources and `arena_fallback_required` is closed by nothing, while Debate — the path that must be refused whenever the question is empirical — has both docs/contracts/debate.md and resources/debate/debate-manifest.schema.json.

The flow states that 02 §2 holds the single definition of `epic_ref_key` and then restates it with a lowercase-hex requirement that 02 §2 does not contain, which for a byte-exact ref name used in expected-old CAS is part of identity, not formatting.

The evidence tree and protocol-snapshot tree are written under `<absolute-project-root>` while the isolation guards in the same section require evidence and session paths to begin with the canonical root, and the two spellings are used interchangeably even though F005 (symlinked project subdirectory) exists precisely because they can differ.

findings.where: docs/contracts/approved-delta.md §8 ("Parity with the Traycer suite") vs 02-architecture.md §5 and §10
findings.what: A contract section requires parity with a baseline that the design says is never committed to public Git and never readable by the runtime, and no parity data file ships (only resources/traycer-parity/registry.schema.json), so that section's claim is not re-checkable by anyone outside the author's machine.
